entries.title: Cheap-domain cross-domain diversity bypass
entries.origin: Red Team v4 audit — residual finding accepted at architecture lock
entries.threat: S11b requires HIGH-confidence dossier claims to be corroborated by at least two distinct registrable domains. An attacker who controls the target entity's identity (or is motivated to plant a false biographical claim) can register two cheap, unrelated domains (e.g., a vanity ~.com and an expired ~.org) and mirror the same false content to satisfy the ≥2 distinct registrable domains threshold. The multi-subdomain bypass is already closed; the multi-cheap-registrable-domain bypass is not.
entries.current_mitigation: M11 tier-B operator review for entities with kind in {person_lead, person_partner, org_applicant, org_partner, product}. Operator eyes on every claim in those dossiers; cross-domain diversity is a confidence-tier floor, not an operator-review skip. S11a per-org source-domain allowlist forces any non-allowlisted domain through full operator review regardless of entity kind.
entries.residual_gap: Spot-check tier (person_referenced, org_referenced, publication) could accept a HIGH-confidence claim from two cheap unrelated domains without full operator review. The spot-check tier is where this would actually bite.
entries.watch_signal: An actual dossier poisoning incident in a spot-check-tier entity, OR a second independent audit round flagging this vector with a concrete attack scenario, OR operator observation of suspicious cheap-domain pairs in a dossier refresh diff.
entries.revisit_trigger: v0.2 architecture review, OR any observed incident, OR operator request.

entries.title: M13 bypass normalization drift
entries.origin: Red Team v4 audit — policy residual accepted at architecture lock
entries.threat: M13 is the named escape valve for review-seat family outages. Each use is signed, logged, and carries a rigor-breach flag on the resulting draft. The risk is not a single bypass — it's normalization. Repeated bypass use (e.g., six deadlines in a row where Judge was bypassed) erodes the rigor that the default hard-abort is designed to preserve, and the operator stops reading the rigor-breach flag as a warning and reads it as boilerplate.
entries.current_mitigation: Every M13 authorization writes a HIGH-severity admin-risk ledger entry requiring operator re-type confirmation. Rigor-breach flag appears in every affected rails report + claim-evidence map. 24-hour default / 72-hour ceiling on any single authorization; no auto-renewal — each extension is a new signed authorization. The audit trail is forensically reviewable.
entries.residual_gap: There is no automated pattern detection on bypass frequency. The operator logs capture the data, but nothing currently flags 'bypass N used 4 times in 30 days' as an anomaly. A diligent operator notices; a tired operator under deadline pressure might not.
entries.watch_signal: Operator observation of M13 usage spiking, OR a post-incident review revealing that rigor-breach flags were ignored, OR a pattern detection rule (if added in blueprint Section 4 or 5) firing.
entries.revisit_trigger: When blueprint Section 4 (Logician) or Section 5 (Pipeline) is designed, evaluate whether a monthly bypass-frequency report to operator is warranted. Revisit this entry at that time.
